result.Method of Attack: Weaponized copy of legitimate npm package call-bind with modified package.json and additional malicious files; Preinstall script executes callTo.js which downloads encrypted payload via curl, decrypts it with PowerShell script, executes payload via rundll32, and cleans up traces; Use of social engineering via fake job interviews to lure developers into installing the malicious package
result.Impacted Systems: Software developers' systems using npm on Windows_NT environments
result.Attack Vector: Publishing a near-duplicate malicious package on npm mimicking a legitimate package (call-bind) to exploit trust; Execution of malicious preinstall script during package installation
result.Indicators of Compromise: Malicious package name: call-blockflow; Malicious URL: https://cryptocopedia.com/explorer/search.asp?token=5032; Files involved: callTo.js, dope.bat, towr.ps1, funData.ctr, colfunc.csv, stringh.dat, mod.json; Use of rundll32 to execute exported function SetExpVal with parameter tiend; Rapid publish and unpublish cycle on npm registry; Misspelled description field in package.json (e.g., 'funcion'); Preinstall script pattern: node <file> && del <file>
